<section class="book-reviews-section">

      <p class="page-subtitle">Planned critical reviews of key texts in golf science, biomechanics, and control theory</p>
      <div style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; background: #f3f4f6; border-left: 4px solid #9ca3af; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.95rem; color: #4b5563;">

    <section style="margin-top: 2rem;">
      <h2>Planned Reviews</h2>
      <p style="color: var(--text-light); margin-bottom: 1.5rem;">
        The following books are queued for review. Each review will examine the text's scientific
        foundations and its relationship to the control-affine framework developed on this site.
      </p>
      <div class="reviews-list">

        <article class="review-card" style="opacity: 0.65; border-left: 3px solid var(--accent-secondary);">
          <div class="review-header">
            <h2>The Search for the Perfect Golf Swing</h2>
            <span class="review-date">Cochran &amp; Stobbs, 1968</span>
          </div>
          <div class="review-content">
            <p>
              The foundational scientific study of golf mechanics, based on the Golf Society of Great
              Britain research programme. Introduces the double-pendulum model and first quantitative
              analysis of clubhead speed generation. Essential historical context for any biomechanical
              framework.
            </p>
            <p style="font-style: italic; font-size: 0.9em; color: var(--text-light);">
              Review in progress — examining the double-pendulum assumptions against the
              full control-affine model.
            </p>
          </div>
        </article>

        <article class="review-card" style="opacity: 0.65; border-left: 3px solid var(--accent-secondary);">
          <div class="review-header">
            <h2>The Physics of Golf (Penner)</h2>
            <span class="review-date">A. Raymond Penner, 2003</span>
          </div>
          <div class="review-content">
            <p>
              Comprehensive physics treatment covering ball aerodynamics, club-ball impact, shaft
              dynamics, and putting mechanics. Penner's treatment of shaft bending is directly
              relevant to the ZTCF framework's elastic shaft modes.
            </p>
            <p style="font-style: italic; font-size: 0.9em; color: var(--text-light);">
              Review queued — Reports on Progress in Physics, 66(2), 131–171.
            </p>
          </div>
        </article>

        <article class="review-card" style="opacity: 0.65; border-left: 3px solid var(--accent-secondary);">
          <div class="review-header">
            <h2>Underactuated Robotics</h2>
            <span class="review-date">Russ Tedrake, MIT OpenCourseWare</span>
          </div>
          <div class="review-content">
            <p>
              The graduate-level text underpinning much of the control theory applied here.
              Chapters on trajectory optimisation, LQR, and differential flatness are directly
              referenced in the AffineDrift articles. Review will focus on underactuated dynamics
              and its application to the drift-dominated swing.
            </p>
          </div>
        </article>

      </div>
    </section>
  </div>
</section>
